posts.name: Killswitch
posts.cooked:
Dr Tremata also has the same effect.

I don't see this as evidence for or against anything, really. We don't know what her story is, but whether or not she chooses to allow her misfortunes dictate her future is independant of what happens to Taurus.

I see it as just being a danger for them or the hero they speak with to give them information.   Private Investigators also aren't always on the side of the law.   Their goal is to gather information on what they got hired for and at times will cross the law to get that.

You don't think his tendency to bend the rules is curious? It's much easier to get the job done if he doesn't have to abide by them. As a criminal, the only one he has to answer to is himself.

It's possible they are so advanced they take future actions into account when judging ppl, but Im not sure there is enough evidence to back it up. You almost kinda have to assume it is past actions being shown.

posts.name: Killswitch
posts.cooked:
Keep in mind, Tremata deals with the environment, so it makes sense that she is a scientist. There aren't too many moral issues with her line of work. She's just doing her research, and doesn't at all seem to mind that the heroes are bothering her to find out what they're up against.

Taurus, on the other hand is shown to pull the old "good cop/bad cop" routine, as suggested by his flavor text:

"I'm here to get information," Tony stated, calmly holstering his revolver. "You will tell me what I want to know. Now, how do you want this to go?"

That's my thoughts as far as that goes. Sure they operate similarly, but their professions and quotes suggest they have different personalities.
